scope: 39 available stranded members individually reviewed; two parent DEB verdicts retained as instructed. Two named Ruby members were not present in the supplied DEB member listing or extraction and have no invented verdict/marker.
method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md before authoring.
Verified each member SHA-256; collected atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none --format json and cleave facts before judging.
Read complete PHP/ASP source, read the JSP embedded in the WAR, unpacked the gem without executing Ruby, and traced Mettle request/command and capture handlers.

Gunzip and inspect all 30 GoAhead ELFs individually with rizin and LLVM disassembly/relocations; compare actual code paths to included C source. SPARC required LLVM because the installed Rizin renderer produced empty instructions.
Re-ran atomscan for every available member with the final rule set, verified hashes and coverage, and wrote exactly one sidecar per available member. No payload was executed.
limits: No deployed-host context or proof of an authorized engagement was supplied. Known pentest provenance does not change the shell payloads into ordinary administration programs.

The two Mettle distribution containers are BENIGN as the supplied cached library and its data archive: their Ruby API reads/configures and returns bytes without an install/require-time agent launch. Accurate hostile findings on agents/sniffers are retained under the queue exception. This does not re-judge the enclosing confirmed DEB.
The PHP shell has a source syntax defect. The WAR has a different, working unauthenticated JSP from the neighboring faulty JSP source.
Gzip compression and flat ELF process-image layouts were not treated as evidence of concealed intent; indirect PHP request dispatch was traced explicitly.
changes: Mettle ELF identity combines three exact function-name entries scoped to .strtab; ordinary network clients, off-section mentions, and incomplete marker sets do not satisfy the hostile composite.
Mettle sniffer detection uses the existing build-path identity across ELF/Mach-O and no longer suppresses real capture capability by bin/sniffer or payload-package path.

Mbed TLS certificate parsing, private-key parsing, and handshake API references now have crypto/TLS homes. Generic parsers no longer assert server credential-file material. The TLS command-listener consumer follows the relocated handshake rule.

Moved 18 existing key representation rules out of the legacy asymmetric-key branch; every matcher, effective default, confidence and severity was compared with HEAD and preserved. Exact consumers and two fixture catalogs follow the moved IDs. No selectors of the legacy key/asymmetric directories were found. Crypto ancestor membership is preserved for these moves; the newly relocated parsing API signals appropriately enter crypto consumers.

checks.native_capture_tls_controls: 12 inert ELF positive/near-miss controls pass, including renamed packaged agents/sniffers, missing roles, off-section mentions, generic libpcap and parsing-only exports.
checks.key_migration: 18 old/new rule objects and defaults compared and identical after reference normalization. Documentation key-downgrade fixtures retain the moved finding. Both moved WIF format and roll-up match the existing WIF fixture. The retired multi-store ID in that historical catalog is absent in current rules.
checks.final_repository_validation: Required final action: make validate; outcome reported in the final response.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/php/shell.php
members.marker_note: Laudanum PHP shell: request-command payload with syntax defect
members.behavior: POST command is assigned to $command, processed for cd/exit/aliases, then passed to proc_open; stdout/stderr feed session output and the HTML terminal. IP allowlist with 404 fallback and SHA-1 password/session authentication are present. A missing semicolon after the $users array makes these exact bytes fail parsing; it remains an identifiable command-shell payload. Not a privilege-escalation mechanism.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/asp/shell.asp
members.marker_note: Laudanum ASP shell: IP-gated HTTP commands execute through WSH
members.behavior: The client address must equal 1.2.3.4 or the page returns 404 and ends. On form submission, cmd is passed to WScript.Shell.Exec, and StdOut.ReadAll is HTML-escaped into the response. Exec starts a requested program; shell parsing requires the operator to supply cmd.exe /c. This is an IP-gated web command shell, not an outbound reverse shell.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/wordpress/templates/php-reverse-shell.php
members.marker_note: WordPress reverse shell: request-selected TCP peer receives shell I/O
members.behavior: HTTP POST ip/port fields choose the callback, defaulting to 10.2.2.1:8888. Optionally forks and setsid, changes to /, resets umask, opens fsockopen, starts uname -a; w; id; /bin/sh -i with proc_open, then stream_select relays socket input to child stdin and stdout/stderr back to the socket. No durable persistence or elevation is established.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/php/php-reverse-shell.php
members.marker_note: PHP reverse shell: fixed TCP peer receives interactive shell I/O
members.behavior: Uses the fixed private address 10.2.2.1:8888. Optional pcntl_fork/setsid detaches; chdir and umask prepare the process. fsockopen connects and proc_open launches uname -a; w; id; /bin/sh -i. The stream_select loop bridges that socket and child standard streams. This is an outbound shell, not HTTP task polling.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/wordpress/templates/shell.php
members.marker_note: WordPress shell: POST commands reach proc_open; login gate disabled
members.behavior: Includes ipcheck.php, whose IP allowlist/404 gate applies if that dependency is present. The authentication-enforcement branch is replaced with if(true); POST command drives cwd changes or proc_open. The child output is saved to session state and returned in the web terminal. Presence of a password form does not restore the disabled login gate.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/jsp/cmd.war
members.marker_note: Laudanum WAR: unauthenticated HTTP cmd reaches Runtime.exec
members.behavior: The actual cmd.jsp inside the WAR reads request.getParameter("cmd"), passes that exact value to Runtime.getRuntime().exec, and writes child stdout lines to the HTTP response. The embedded JSP has no authentication/IP filter and differs from the neighboring warfiles/cmd.jsp, which has a broken filter and syntax defect. WEB-INF/web.xml declares the JSP servlet.

members.name: c3f630/usr/share/laudanum/php/hidden.php
members.marker_note: Laudanum hidden shell: request imports drive arbitrary function calls
members.behavior: The only executable statements are @extract($_REQUEST) and @die($ctime($atime)). Default extract overwrite semantics let a requester choose both function name and argument, including system with an OS command, and return its result. Error suppression and indirect dispatch obscure the execution sink; there is no credential or IP check.

members.name: f1a842/usr/share/metasploit-framework/vendor/bundle/ruby/3.3.0/cache/metasploit_payloads-mettle-1.0.46.gem
members.marker_note: Mettle gem: payload distribution API; no install-time execution
members.behavior: The gem metadata declares no executables, native extensions, or post-install hook. Its three Ruby files define a selector/configuration API: read returns local payload bytes, to_binary optionally patches DEFAULT_OPTS with generated argv, and load_extension also returns bytes. It does not spawn an agent on require or install. The packaged native Mettle agents register C2 transports and TLV handlers; sys_process_execute extracts requested executable/arguments and hands them to process_create_from_executable[_buf]. The sniffer registers capture-start/stop/dump handlers and uses libpcap. Those payload behaviors remain accurately hostile findings. As the supplied cached distribution library, the wrapper is judged BENIGN; no active deployment or authorization context was supplied.

members.name: f1a842/data.tar.gz
members.marker_note: Mettle data archive: packaged payloads; Ruby only returns bytes
members.behavior: This is the hash-verified data.tar.gz member extracted from the Mettle gem, not the Debian data.tar. It contains the same three byte-dispensing Ruby API files and 61 cross-platform agent/capture artifacts. In the x86_64 ELF agent, main reaches mettle_start; C2 setup registers transports and stdapi, and the TLV request dispatcher invokes the selected handler. sys_process_execute reads the request fields and creates a child/channel. The sniffer main registers capture/start/stop/dump handlers. The stock payload inventory is judged BENIGN in this distribution context, while its payload findings remain hostile under the queue exception. There is no install hook or unexpected wrapper execution.

members.name: f1a842/usr/share/metasploit-framework/data/exploits/CVE-2017-17562/goahead-cgi-bind-linux-glibc-aarch64.so.gz
members.marker_note: GoAhead aarch64 bind payload: preload forks socket-to-shell
members.behavior: Independently gunzipped and inspected the aarch64 ELF, including loader initialization and call/relocation paths. The constructor removes LD_PRELOAD and forks; the child binds INADDR_ANY on port 55555, listens with backlog 5, accepts one client and closes the listener. The accepted/connected descriptor is duplicated onto 0, 1 and 2, then execl tries a list of /bin and /usr/bin shells until one succeeds. Parent/failure paths exit. This is a load-triggered bind shell payload; gzip and placeholder configuration are packaging, not an encrypted hidden program. No elevation or durable persistence is established.

The constructor removes LD_PRELOAD and forks; the child parses the patchable 000.000.000.000 and 55555 strings, opens a stream socket and retries connect up to ten times. The accepted/connected descriptor is duplicated onto 0, 1 and 2, then execl tries a list of /bin and /usr/bin shells until one succeeds. Parent/failure paths exit. This is a load-triggered reverse shell payload; gzip and placeholder configuration are packaging, not an encrypted hidden program. No elevation or durable persistence is established.
